summary: The portfolio reflects a late-cycle, stagflationary regime call: Core PCE at 3.3–3.4%, a hawkish Fed with 50%+ September hike probability, a bear steepener yield curve (10Y at 4.78%, 30Y at 5.25%), and geopolitical energy shock from U.S.-Iran conflict that structurally supports Energy (MPC) while compressing duration-sensitive growth assets. The 10-name growth book expresses the 'silicon to steel' great sector rotation — overweighting Energy (MPC), Healthcare quality compounders (AMGN, REGN, VRTX), Financials benefiting from curve steepening (SPGI, BAC), and AI-essential software/cybersecurity (CRWD, CRM, SNOW) with a gold miner kicker (NEM) — while the 5-name defensive sleeve (GLD, SCHD, BRK.B, IEF, KO) provides recession insurance, inflation hedging, and quality income ballast at a DefensiveScore of 4. Key changes from yesterday: JPM replaced by BAC (BAC is explicitly in the momentum screen at 3M +16.4% vs SPY +12.0 while JPM is not; BAC wins on today's numbers); MRK dropped to resolve a 4-name Healthcare concentration that would have violated the max-3-per-sector rule; NEM and SNOW carried on 1-day momentum confirmation; PANW challenger rejected as it remains below the 50-DMA at -15.8% off its high, while CRWD (above 50-DMA, 'best quarter ever') definitively wins the cybersecurity head-to-head. The dominant risk being underwritten is a September hike + hot August CPI combo that compresses multiples across the growth book simultaneously — the IEF position and elevated SCHD/GLD/BRK.B defensive sleeve are sized to absorb that scenario without catastrophic portfolio drawdown.
diversificationNote: The 10-name growth book spans 5 distinct GICS sectors: Energy (MPC), Information Technology (CRWD, CRM, SNOW — at the 3-name maximum), Health Care (AMGN, REGN, VRTX — at the 3-name maximum), Financials (SPGI, BAC), and Materials (NEM); the IT sleeve spans three distinct end markets — cybersecurity platform (CRWD), enterprise AI software (CRM), and data cloud infrastructure (SNOW) — limiting single-factor crowding; the defensive sleeve spans four distinct exposures: physical gold (GLD), broad dividend/quality income ETF (SCHD), quality compounder equity (BRK.B), intermediate duration Treasuries (IEF), and consumer staples (KO).
